lines.en: Four days had passed since we visited the 'Castle of Reincarnators.'
According to what I had confirmed through [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint], the other companions had finished their Middle Island scenarios and were ready to enter the next scenario.
And I was looking at my smartphone screen.
―Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World(Final Version).TXT
Perhaps at the end of this file lay the 'epilogue' of the story I had wanted so desperately to see.
And was that all? If I was lucky, there might be more information about this third round.
Instructions telling me how to act and carry out the scenarios to reach a safe ending.
「What if that sto ry ends in tra ge dy?」
What if 'Final Version' meant 'it will never change again'?
「Can you cha nge it?」
What if reading it instead fixed every future in place?
“Kim Dokja.”
I looked up to find Han Sooyoung watching me, a bandage wrapped around her left hand.
Almost the only being in this world besides me who had read 'Ways of Survival.'
What would Han Sooyoung have done in my place?
If she were me, would she open this file?
“What are you staring at?”
“No, nothing.”
I turned off the smartphone screen.
Perhaps someday I would want to read this story.
But not now.
The 'epilogue' I wanted to read probably was not in this file.
Having finished tending her equipment, Han Sooyoung hopped down from the bed where she had been sitting and spoke.
“Let's get moving. Keep dawdling and that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk will get ahead of us.”
“There's someone I need to meet before we leave.”
“Who?”
“Looks like he's just arrived.”
With a knock, someone opened the door.

The first thing I noticed was a thick strand of brown prayer beads around his neck. Firm, lean muscles showed here and there beneath gray monastic robes. He was a warrior monk (武僧) who had trained relentlessly for a very long time.
“I have come to escort you, benefactor.”
I nodded and answered.
“Take us to your king.”
『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.
According to my interpretation as the foremost authority on 'Ways of Survival,' the 'three ways' in the title referred to the three protagonists who appeared in the novel.
The first was the regressor Yoo Joonghyuk.
The second was the returnee Jang Hayoung.
And the third was······.
―There's another protagonist?
After hearing my explanation, Han Sooyoung asked through [Midday Tryst].
Come to think of it, I supposed Han Sooyoung wouldn't know details like these.
She had only read a hundred-odd installments, after all······.
―Well, to write three thousand installments, it'd be hard to milk just one protagonist for all of them.
······Needlessly perceptive.
―Anyway, three protagonists? That's a shortcut to a novel flopping.
I could not think of anything to say.
And now that flop of a novel was even ruining our reality.
―The owner of this castle is the 'third,' right?
―Right.
―How big a role does he have in 'Ways of Survival'? As big as Yoo Joonghyuk's?
―Not that big. Yoo Joonghyuk's the main one, after all.
In fact, most of the story's more than three thousand installments unfolded around Yoo Joonghyuk.
Even calling the other two 'protagonists' merely followed the narration within the work.
―But the other two are no less monstrous than Yoo Joonghyuk. Especially now, the 'third protagonist' is stronger than Yoo Joonghyuk.
―······Stronger than that Yoo Joonghyuk?
I nodded and looked around the empty meditation chamber.
This room was where reincarnators practiced austerities. A room to soothe minds exhausted and worn down by countless cycles of rebirth.
Murmured recitations of scripture came from here and there, but the king was nowhere to be seen.
“Where is the King of Reincarnators?”
“The king is already here.”
“All I see are fake monks.”
The warrior monk answered Han Sooyoung bluntly.
“He is everywhere, and nowhere.”
“I doubt you invited us here to play word games.”
“He does not speak with beings unqualified to see him.”
“How amusing. Are you throwing us a koan?”
Han Sooyoung smiled, raising just one corner of her mouth.
I studied the warrior monk's mysterious expression, then spoke.
“If the king truly is everywhere, that would mean anyone can become 'king.'”
Kiiiiing!
[Unbreakable Faith] rang in my hand, and almost simultaneously, its tip shot toward the warrior monk's throat.
Tzzzzzzzt!
The sword tip, radiating fierce magic power, stopped right in front of the warrior monk. As though blocked by an invisible wall. The warrior monk was smiling.
[What a provocative solution. Correct. Anyone who attains enlightenment can become a Buddha.]
A True Voice reverberating through the entire space.
I withdrew my sword and looked at the warrior monk. An ethereal aura flowed from his entire body. In his pupils, now pure white, lay the shadow of a mandala rotating counterclockwise.
This warrior monk was probably one of the countless incarnations of the King of Reincarnators.
[But you will not be able to proceed through the scenarios that way forever, ■■ Apostle who bears the weight of salvation.]
“Don't speak as though you know everything about how I do things.”
I no longer thought of 'Ways of Survival' as merely a novel, or of my companions as mere 'characters.'
But that resolve was not a declaration that I would stop using the information I knew.
“Pleased to meet you, Mandala’s Guardian.”
Even with [Fourth Wall] active, I felt considerable pressure.
The stirrings of a gentle Status shimmered before me. The great mind behind the warrior monk was revealing itself in full before my eyes.
The one who ruled the oldest Dark Fault in the world.
Even <Eden>'s Metatron or the highest-ranking Demon Kings of the Demon Realm could not oppose this being on this island. The instant our eyes met, sparks flew in the air.
[The 'Fourth Wall' twitches its nonexistent eyebrows.]
[The 'Wall that Decides Samsara' shows curiosity toward you.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
The third Wall, after Jang Hayoung's [Unidentifiable Wall] and Metatron's [Wall that Divides Good and Evil].
Mandala’s Guardian was the owner of the [Wall that Decides Samsara].
[A 'Fragment of the Final Wall.' Nirvana must be trapped inside it too, yes?]
“Yes.”
[That child could have become a fine bodhisattva, but, unfortunately, meeting you led them astray from their Buddhist path.]
“Well, they seem quite content with their life.”
It was then that Han Sooyoung interrupted.
“Wait. ······Are you Buddha-nim?”
[There are many kinds of Buddha in this world, and I am one of them.]
Han Sooyoung looked dumbfounded.
Well, a constellation claiming to be Buddha-nim had appeared. It was understandable. The gently smiling Buddha-nim looked at me and spoke.
[I have watched your stories for a very long time, bodhisattvas.]
“I don't think you've ever sponsored me.”
[Some constellations flaunt their gaze to wield power, while others exist so quietly one hardly knows they are there. True giving comes not from sponsorship, but from steadfast contemplation.]
“What a long-winded way to say you watch the broadcast for free. So, what do you want from me?”
[Want? Do you think I want something from you, bodhisattva?]
I looked at the great bell in the center of the meditation chamber. Inside the transparent bell was a small soul enveloped in dazzling light.
I already knew whose soul it was.
“You agreed to reincarnate Yoo Sangah-ssi. Even though I never asked you to.”
“You invited us here and gave us lodging. Again, without my ever asking.”
[It was merely part of the fruits of Buddhahood (佛果).]
“I've learned something from dealing with constellations all this time. No constellation does anyone a favor without a price.”
[Your judgment is hasty, bodhisattva. Only one who can believe in exceptions to everything can fathom the end of the scenarios.]
I stared quietly at the warrior monk, then glanced at the bell in the center of the meditation chamber and spoke.
“Do not bind the incarnation Yoo Sangah to this island. She is far more valuable than you think.”
[All beings reincarnated on this island are bound to it.]
I shook my head.
“As you just said, isn't there an exception to everything? She can succeed Nirvana. Make the incarnation Yoo Sangah your [Arhat].”
Arhat (阿羅漢).
Seekers who traversed the worlds of the scenarios, reincarnating again and again without being bound to 'Reincarnation Island.'
“If you do that, I'll make a deal with you.”
[A deal. What do you believe I want?]
“Don't you want to stop the Great War of Saints and Demons?”
[How vain. I have no interest in contradictory Stories such as Good and Evil.]
“Even if that contradictory Story wrecks your island?”
The warrior monk's eyes curved gently, as though he was intrigued.
Mandala’s Guardian was neither Good nor Evil. If one had to describe him, he was closer to emptiness (空). He could hardly welcome the growing influence of Good and Evil in his own territory.
“I'll try to stop the 'Great War of Saints and Demons.'”
[You think that possible with your strength?]
My Stories answered for me.
[The Giant Story 'Demon Realm's Spring' roars!]
[The Giant Story 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth' growls!]
As the two Giant Stories activated, the air around us trembled uneasily.
If my guess was right, Mandala’s Guardian could not refuse my proposal. He could not enter this 'Great War of Saints and Demons' himself.
Being neither Good nor Evil, he had no grounds to join this fight.
[······Taking the incarnation named 'Yoo Sangah' as my 'Arhat.' Is that all you wish for, bodhisattva?]
“One more thing.”
[What a greedy bodhisattva.]
“Let my nebula begin the 'Great War of Saints and Demons' in the region we choose. As the island's owner, you should be able to intervene that much.”
For an instant, I felt faint magic power stirring throughout the temple.
A display of Status, as though warning me. It was neither threatening nor murderous, but carried an aura that somehow felt unapproachable.
[The 'Fourth Wall' activates strongly!]
[The 'Wall that Decides Samsara' smacks its lips.]
At length, Mandala’s Guardian nodded.
[I will accept your conditions, bodhisattva. But your entire nebula cannot begin in the Main Island region you desire.]
“Then please, at least the incarnation Lee Gilyoung and the incarnation Shin Yoosung.”
[Hmm······ Where would you have me send them?]
“Next City.”
[Next City······ Oh dear, bodhisattva, surely you don't······.]
Mandala’s Guardian would have realized my intention.
The Main Island of 'Reincarnation Island' was a place where forgotten third-generation Stories were preserved like specimens.
Third-generation Stories had a far wider spectrum than those of the first and second generations, so depending on where one started, one might gain an utterly unexpected Story.
Regardless of where the others began, I had to make sure the two children began in 'Next City.'
[······In return, the rest of your companions must begin wherever I choose.]
“Understood.”
At my reply, Han Sooyoung, who had been watching beside me, gave me a look.
―Hey, what if that fake monk sends us somewhere strange?
As he watched us bicker, a peculiar smile formed on the warrior monk's lips.
[Bodhisattva, I like your story very much······ But the Stories you have built are still insufficient to oppose the other nebulas participating in the Great War of Saints and Demons.]
Perhaps the word 'insufficient' had offended her. Han Sooyoung sneered.
“······Haven't you heard how we smashed <Olympus>?”
[The Stories you have built are unparalleled, bodhisattvas, but they have yet to weather the passage of time.]
And the next moment, Han Sooyoung and I were engulfed in a sudden light.
[The constellation 'Mandala’s Guardian' has consented to the scenario transfer.]
[Scenario transfer begins!]
······Just like that?
I was a little surprised, but quickly steadied myself.
At last, we were going to the region of the third Giant Story that would complete the Climax (轉).
The other companions on the Middle Islands were probably being transferred with me.
When I turned my head, Han Sooyoung was looking at me.
“Kim Dokja.”
Reflexively, I reached toward Han Sooyoung and answered.
“Do your best. I'll come find you soon.”
“······Yeah, right.”
The instant Han Sooyoung's fist struck my hand, her body turned into a shaft of light.
Watching her fading afterimage, I felt anew that she had become my companion.
As Yoo Joonghyuk had, Han Sooyoung had now become someone I needed for my ending.
She had helped me so much until now.
So this time, it was my turn to repay her.
「But Kim Dokja did not know then.」
It was then that the smartphone screen began to shine brightly.
Sentences from a page I did not know appeared before my eyes one line at a time, like ominous foreshadowing.
「That when Kim Dokja met her again······.」
No, wait.
「Fifty years would already have passed.」
Fifty years? What on earth did that mean?
Through my fading vision, I saw the smile on the warrior monk's lips.
―Bodhisattva, try enduring time.
[Beginning transfer to the Main Island!]
[The 'Wall that Decides Samsara' examines your Story information!]
[Examination complete.]
[The scenario regions for you and your companions have been determined.]
The last thing I heard was the following message.
[Sub-scenario― 'Genre Selection' has begun!]
Looking down at the black liquid in the transparent cup, Ricardo recalled memories from long ago.
「“Even fifty years of training would not be enough for you to become a court magician.”」
When he first learned magic.
「“Your constitution is not suited to becoming a sage.”」
When he received lessons from the greatest sage in the Kaizenix Archipelago.
「“Your hands are ill suited to wielding a sword.”」
And when he first held a sword at the royal swordsmanship training academy, too.
「“Some lives are like that. What matters is not becoming discouraged, but pressing steadily onward.”」
Ricardo's father, Berchen von Kaizenix, had said that.
It was no comfort. How could someone with neither talent nor anything he wanted to do take comfort in such words?
Press steadily onward even without talent? What could he possibly become by living that way?
Ricardo drank every day. He ran with the archipelago's hoodlums, took drugs, and squandered his family's wealth on gambling.
He had loved, too. Once.
She was an older woman, the most beautiful in the archipelago. But when she married his eldest brother, that love ended too.
Staring into the liquid in his cup, Ricardo murmured.
“Let's die.”
It was the first time in his life he had mustered any courage.
He held the cup lightly and drained it as though drinking wine. It soon took effect. Ricardo's complexion darkened, and his arm fell limply.
Then, exactly four hours later.
Someone opened their eyes in Ricardo's body.
I had read quite a few stories besides 'Ways of Survival.' As a child, I read the good books my mother recommended, and once I grew a little older, I chose books for myself.
For the record, the first webnovel I ever read began with the protagonist chattering about their misfortunes, dying, and waking again.
Just like now.
“Bleeuuurgh!”
“Prince Ricardo-nim! Are you all right?”
Someone patted my back, and I heaved up vomit for a long time.
I wiped my mouth and raised my head to find a mirror.
Before me was a pale, handsome face with fine features.
······It was definitely my face, yet somehow unfamiliar.
Who was I?
「“As you know, I'm not a prophet. In fact, I'm very far from anything like that.”」
I.
「“I'm not the Demon King of Salvation either. Or the King of a Kingless World.”」
「“Twenty-eight······ No, I was twenty-eight, and worked at a game company. My hobby was reading webnovels······.”」
[Your Stories resist the Giant Story that constitutes this world setting!]
[The exclusive skill 'Fourth Wall' activates strongly!]
As I slowly closed and reopened my eyes, I felt as though the world were separating.
[The 'Fourth Wall' impedes your immersion in the character.]
[The effect of the 'Fourth Wall' fully preserves your sense of self.]
[The island's probability questions your special privilege.]
The sensations of an unfamiliar body.
This was not my body.
「I am Kim Dokja.」
As my mind abruptly cleared, a sequence of memories fell into place.
I had entered the 'Great War of Saints and Demons' scenario and had just reached the Main Island.
The Main Island consisted of third-generation Stories spanning a wide spectrum. Each Story formed a world setting of a different genre. Then this scene before my eyes······.
“······A possession story.”
Tzzzzzzzzt!
[An utterance incompatible with the world setting has been detected!]
[Sanctions begin!]
I woke again two hours later.
“Prince-nim. Are you all right?”
Someone in my hazy field of vision called to me.
“······Um, could I have some water?”
[You have used language incompatible with the world setting!]
[A penalty will be impo······.]
“Bring me some water.”
“Here you are.”
As I gulped down cold water, I gradually regained my senses.
The fragments of someone else's memories washing over me left my mind in turmoil.
I had entered the body of a person who had already lived for thirty years.
「In some regions of the 'Main Island,' utterances incompatible with the world setting are forbidden.」
Passages from 'Ways of Survival' surfaced dimly. It was a round described only in passing, but 'Ways of Survival' had certainly mentioned a scenario like this—certainly.
A so-called 'possession scenario.'
I had to proceed through the 'Great War of Saints and Demons' from this character's viewpoint.
[Dokkaebis cannot be summoned in this region.]
[Indirect messages from constellations cannot be received in this region.]
······And there were strange restrictions on top of that.
This was not how the 'Great War of Saints and Demons' I knew had unfolded.
“······I'd better gather some information first.”
[You have acted in accordance with the character's attributes.]
[Your understanding of this character increases.]
I immediately began searching my memories of 'Ways of Survival.'
「The Kaizenix Archipelago. The island of heroes who led the Age of Holy Magic.」
No particularly useful information came to mind.
Of all places, a region that barely appeared in 'Ways of Survival.'
Yet it did not feel entirely unfamiliar either······.
Was that because the possessed character's memories had flowed into me?
[You have activated the exclusive skill 'Character List'!]
Normally, I could not see my own Attributes Window.
But if it was the Attributes Window of the person I possessed······.
<Character Information>
Name: Ricardo von Kaizenix (Kim Dokja)
Age: 31
Constellation Sponsor (背後星): None (1 constellation is currently showing interest.)
Exclusive Attribute: Gifted Hoodlum
Exclusive Skills: [Royalty's Outer Appearance Lv.3], [Soliloquy Lv.6], [Roleplay Lv.5]
Stigmas: None
Overall Stats: [Constitution Lv.10], [Strength Lv.10], [Agility Lv.10], [Magic Power Lv.10]
Overall Evaluation: The character you possess is the fourth prince of the Kaizenix Archipelago. Unfortunately, he has no aptitude for swordsmanship, magic, or combat of any kind.
●Currently afflicted with the status condition 'Possession.'
······Why did I have to possess someone like this?
The scenario message had clearly said I would be immersed in a 'character connected to me.'
But what connection could there possibly be between me and a wastrel prince?
Besides, this bastard had been born with Constitution, Strength, and Agility of ten.
The only similarity was our age, more or less······.
“Prince-nim, are you immersed in roleplay again?”
“Roleplay?”
“Last time, you imitated the founding head of the family······ But I've never seen this attire before. You are dressed just like a character from the Earth Chronicles.”
I glanced at the mirror and saw familiar clothes. Strangely, on possessing this body, I had also been transferred with all my equipment. I answered brazenly.
“The attire of a certain Demon King.”
“······A Demon King?”
When I reached into the inner pocket of my coat, I was relieved to feel my equipment still there.
First, I took out my smartphone. To learn about this place, I needed to consult 'Ways of Survival' again······.
Tzzzzzt!
[This item cannot be used because it is incompatible with the world setting.]
······This damned penalty.
However he interpreted my actions, the butler spoke.
“Well, it may be good to enjoy yourself one last time. The king will summon you soon. Until then.”
With only those words, the butler left.
I was left all alone in the small room.
「Kim Dok ja is lone ly」
Yes, at least I had you. What had happened to the others······?
According to the last message I heard, the other companions had most likely come to the same region as me.
First, I opened the scenario window. The accumulated messages came tumbling out.
[You have entered the 'Kaizenix Archipelago' on the 'Main Island.']
[The 'Kaizenix Archipelago' is currently separated in space and time from the conflict regions of the 'Great War of Saints and Demons.']
[Upon resolving this region's sub-scenario, you may proceed to the 'Great War of Saints and Demons.']
I would probably have to raise a military faction here and enter the Great War of Saints and Demons.
In other words, this region would become my foundation for joining the war.
[You cannot view the scenario information yet.]
[This scenario unfolds differently depending on the route you choose.]
The route I chose?
No, but I at least needed to know the failure conditions······.
[You will not fail this scenario unless you die.]
This was another first.
Anyway, it meant I would not fail this scenario as long as I stayed alive?
Sitting on the edge of the bed, I calmly gathered my thoughts.
In this world setting, my name was Ricardo von Kaizenix.
Since this scenario was based on 'possession,' I had to remain fully in character as the prince here.
My first task was to find the other members of <Kim Dokja’s Company>. They were most likely possessing other characters as I was. First I would find them, then······.
“Prince-nim, are you there? It is the knight Bilston.”
No sooner had I thought it than someone knocked on the door.
The knight Bilston Framer.
If Ricardo's memories were correct, he was my bodyguard.
“The king has summoned you.”
But the instant he opened the door and entered, a strange feeling swept over me.
An aging knight in his forties with a white mustache. The man before me certainly had an unfamiliar face. And yet.
[Your Stories react to this character!]
[The exclusive attribute 'Scenario Interpreter' takes effect!]
The man's face was changing little by little.
Though little time had passed, it was a voice I missed as though it had been ages.
「“I once lost a spent cartridge case in the army.”」
The Stories dwelling within the man spoke to me. Their exhausted sentences desperately appealed to me for something.
「“I told myself I would never lose it again.”」
I knew the owner of this Story.
“······Hyunsung-ssi?”
Then Lee Hyunsung looked at me.
[This character does not understand your words.]
“You are Hyunsung-ssi, aren't you?”
[This character does not understand your words.]
[The world setting recommends that you perform your assigned role accurately.]
After staring blankly at me, Lee Hyunsung gave an awkward smile and spoke.
“Hyun―sung? Haha, are you roleplaying again? May I ask what you are imitating?”
Lee Hyunsung seemed not to recognize me at all.
The expression of someone who did not remember anyone like me.
I called his name.
“Sir Bilston.”
“Yes.”
“Do you not know what these clothes are?”
“Hmm······ The attire of demon hunters? Or of the revolutionaries······.”
Though my face was different, I was wearing the white coat I had worn all along.
If this man really was Lee Hyunsung, there was no way he would fail to recognize me.
And yet, the fact that he had not recognized me meant······.
[Activating the exclusive skill 'Character List'!]
<Character Information>
Name: Bilston Framer (???)
Age: 43
Constellation Sponsor (背後星): None
Exclusive Attributes: Loyal Servant, An Honourable Knight
Exclusive Skills: [Rapid Reaction Force Lv.8], [Archipelago's Royal Swordsmanship Lv.8]······.
Stigmas: None
Overall Stats: [Constitution Lv.80], [Strength Lv.80], [Agility Lv.80], [Magic Power Lv.80]

Overall Evaluation: Once, two souls lived in this body. He was a knight of the kingdom, and also someone's shield. The shield waited for its master. It waited, and waited again. After many long years, the shield's master finally appeared, but now the shield could no longer fulfill its role.
Reading the Attributes Window's explanation over and over, I recalled the warning of One Invincible Fist, Yoo Hoseong.
―When you reach the Main Island, beware of 'Giant Stories.'
―But I can handle Giant Stories now.
―That isn't what I mean. There, you will fight a Giant Story itself.
Only now did I think I understood what he had meant.
When I raised my head, I felt the vast probability surrounding the entire archipelago move. Something was watching me from there. Something that was neither a constellation nor a Demon King.
[The Giant Story 'Kaizenix Archipelago' gazes at you greedily.]
I clenched my fists and bit my lip.
Unaware of any of this, Lee Hyunsung kept muttering something.
“Hmm, if you are not a revolutionary either, perhaps from another empire······.”
The Lee Hyunsung I knew had already been swallowed by this world and disappeared.
All the way to the audience chamber, I kept talking to Bilston.
“Sir Bilston. Do you perhaps lose things often? For example, spent cartridge cases······.”
“Pardon?”
[For using language incompatible with the world setting······.]
“I mean, have you ever lost a portable magic bomb······?”
“Do I look like such a pathetic fool?”
I had no idea what to say.

That stiff gait, that firm chest, that clueless expression. He was unmistakably Lee Hyunsung······ Yet according to 'Character List,' this was not Lee Hyunsung, but 'Bilston Framer,' a character of this world setting.
I reread the 'Overall Evaluation' section of Character List.
―Once, two souls lived in this body. He was a knight of the kingdom, and also someone's shield.
The 'knight of the kingdom' would mean 'Bilston Framer,' the original owner of the body, while the 'shield' undoubtedly referred to Lee Hyunsung.
―The shield waited for its master. It waited, and waited again. After many long years, the shield's master finally appeared, but now the shield could no longer fulfill its role.
This was the important part. I understood that Lee Hyunsung had waited for the other companions.
The problem was the number. Exactly how much time did the Overall Evaluation mean by 'a long time'?
“Prince-nim?”
Looking at the man gazing at me with dull eyes, I was filled with mixed emotions.
In this situation, there were only two things I could be sure of.
One, Lee Hyunsung had entered the scenario before me.
Two, the Giant Story of this world had consumed Lee Hyunsung, and his sense of self had vanished.
[The Giant Story 'Kaizenix Archipelago' smacks its lips at you.]
[The 'Fourth Wall' glares at the 'Kaizenix Archipelago.']
Then had everyone else, without [Fourth Wall], ended up like Lee Hyunsung?
“Prince-nim. Is something wrong?”
I looked quietly into Bilston's large eyes.
This character was certainly Lee Hyunsung.
But could I still call him Lee Hyunsung now?
“I am sorry, Sir Bilston.”
“Pardon? What suddenly brings this······?”
“I seem to have put you through far too much. I know how hard you have worked to protect me.”
These words were not meant for Bilston Framer.
“I always used being busy as an excuse to neglect you. Even though you saved my life so many times.”

Lee Hyunsung had helped me many times on the way to this scenario. There had been chances for heartfelt conversations with him, too. But, as always, I had kept putting them off, using preparations for the scenarios as an excuse.
I believed we understood each other without needing to speak.
I thought the Stories of our battles together proved it for us.
And this was the result.
Whatever he had thought of my words, Bilston wiped his nose and looked at the view beyond the corridor.
“Prince-nim, you truly have a warm heart.”
[The character 'Bilston Framer' is moved by you.]
······You weren't the one I wanted to move, though.
We walked down the corridor in silence.
Portraits of successive kings hung along the passage in order. One in particular caught my eye: a man raising a broken sword in a storm.
―Founding head of the family, Storm King Ulysses Kaizenix I.
I stopped for a moment to study the painting.
“It has also been my honor to serve you all my life, Prince-nim.”
I turned to find Bilston beginning to speak, his eyes brimming with tears. Looking toward the distant castle battlements, he continued.
“Do you remember? When you were only seven, Prince-nim, I nearly lost you.”
“My heart still drops when I think of you hanging precariously from the battlements. And do you think that was all? When you were thirteen, you went to the privy and······.”
No, this man······ He was far too much like Lee Hyunsung.
“And yet, Prince-nim, you worry for this lowly servant until the very end······.”
“The very end?”
Bilston looked at me sadly, then averted his eyes.
“······We have arrived. Please enter.”

Before I knew it, the doors of the audience chamber stood before us. They opened, revealing royal guards lined up on either side of a carpet. In their midst stood the guard captain, wearing a silver crest.
“Sir Bilston, why are you so late?”
“I was exchanging my final farewells with the prince.”
There was more than one thing I wanted to challenge in that conversation, but the atmosphere made it hard to speak.
Bilston, who had been on the verge of tears moments earlier, now wore a stern knight's expression. The two glowering gazes clashed in the air.
The captain of the royal guard spoke.
“Farewells? Quite a luxury for someone guilty of high treason.”
“Watch your tongue.”
Both took combat stances at once.
Bilston drew a bastard sword, and the guard captain······ Huh?
······Why did that person have that sword?
The sword in the captain's hand was one I knew all too well.
Because I had personally gathered the materials to have it made for someone.
